description: We are a dedicated team passionate about building practical and innovative solutions. Our main interests lie in solving real-world problems, exploring new technologies, and creating impactful projects from start to finish. We enjoy collaborating, learning through hands-on building, and pushing creative boundaries throughout this event.
summary:
The Quiet Explorers: Abandoned, but Not Forgotten is an interactive website that tells the stories of spacecraft and scientific instruments left across the solar system. Through 17 scenes, visitors travel from Earth to the Moon, Mars, the asteroid belt and beyond, discovering missions such as Apollo, Pathfinder and Sojourner, Opportunity and Dawn.

The project addresses the challenge by turning space exploration history into an engaging visual journey. Visitors can explore 3D scenes, read mission stories and follow links to source material. They can scroll at their own pace or choose a guided demo with adjustable playback.

The project is important because it brings attention to the machines—and the people behind them—that expanded our understanding of the universe. By combining storytelling with interactive visuals, it invites a wider audience to appreciate the lasting scientific legacy of space exploration.
details:
The Quiet Explorers: Abandoned, but Not Forgotten is a website about the spacecraft and equipment that have helped us explore the solar system. We wanted to give people a way to discover not just where these machines went, but what they did and why their missions mattered.

The story moves from Earth to the Moon, Mars, the asteroid belt and beyond. Visitors can scroll through it themselves or watch a guided demo, pausing or changing the speed whenever they want. They can also drag the 3D scenes to see them from different angles and open a separate explorer for a closer look at selected models.

We built the project with React, TypeScript, Three.js and React Three Fiber. We used NASA resources, an attributed third-party Pathfinder and Sojourner model, and photo-textured illustrative terrain. The website also includes links to sources for visitors who want to learn more.

Our creative approach was to treat the spacecraft as the subjects of a journey, rather than simply presenting a list of mission facts. We considered ease of navigation, mobile use, readable text and accessibility, including a reading mode for people who prefer reduced motion or cannot use WebGL.

The scenes are illustrations, not live views or exact reconstructions. We hope the project encourages people to look more closely at the technology and discoveries behind space exploration.
